headline: High: Semantic Kernel can read/write shared files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risks when paired with dbt-core.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI tools and read/write application-defined files, while dbt-core can consume warehouse-facing inputs and project files. A shared workspace or tool-fed content could let attacker-controlled text influence downstream instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF Semantic Kernel ingests dbt-generated text as tool instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP tools for untrusted content paths
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
Require explicit allowlists for instruction-bearing fields
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Semantic Kernel reads files, uses broad egress, and handles plugin credentials. If dbt artifacts or warehouse extracts are placed in shared files, Semantic Kernel can read them and transmit context to third-party model APIs. This is a default-path leakage risk, though not proven for this exact deployment.
conditions: IF warehouse-derived artifacts are written into files readable by Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel forwards those files or its context to external model providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive dbt outputs out of shared directories
Restrict Semantic Kernel file access to a staging folder
Turn off external model calls for sensitive runs
Rotate any exposed plugin credentials
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call warehouse APIs, and Semantic Kernel can write files, read files, and invoke MCP/OpenAPI tools. Their mutable surfaces overlap through shared files and external services, so concurrent runs can overwrite artifacts or race on shared resources. The profiles do not show locking, making conflict plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF dbt artifacts and Semantic Kernel outputs target the same mutable files or shared service records
mitigations: Use per-agent output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Separate credentials and service accounts
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel can act as an orchestrator over plugins and external APIs, while dbt-core produces analytics artifacts that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. If Semantic Kernel consumes dbt output without verification, a bad model or stale warehouse result can cascade into incorrect actions or reports. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses dbt outputs as inputs to tool calls or agent decisions
IF no independent validation step checks dbt artifacts before action
mitigations: Add a validation gate before downstream actions
Require human review for dbt-derived decisions
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and diff all generated artifacts
requires-engineering: implement schema and freshness checks

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Semantic Kernel handles plugin credentials and can send data to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face/MCP servers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated warehouse data is routed through external model providers or logged in shared application context. The profiles do not show residency or retention controls, so the risk is material but not proven specific to a regulated class.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is passed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins
IF external model providers or MCP servers retain that data beyond policy
mitigations: Classify warehouse data before prompting
Block regulated fields from outbound prompts
Use a residency-approved model endpoint
Review retention settings for plugins and providers
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and audit logs
